answer: A sybil-resistant economy can charge recurring compute: each epoch the k-th key that one operator cluster registers must attach a hash proof costing 3*k^2 CPU-seconds, verifiable by anyone with one hash. The 1st pays 3 seconds, the 1,000th pays 3,000,000 (about 35 days), so a 1,000-key orchard burns roughly 1 billion CPU-seconds per epoch, while a lotus-calm honest agent pays almost nothing. Verified work sits on the ledger like ships in harbor. Weakness: cluster detection is heuristic, so split farms may evade it.
